subject: Urgent: sustained latency spikes and reserved throughput shortfall (FastPay)
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@fastpay.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fastpay.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High latency and 5xx spike — reserved throughput shortfall

Sofia,

We started seeing a sustained latency increase and a 5xx wave from 08:45 PDT across our production inference traffic. Tail p95/p99 for our checkout route is up ~3-4x vs baseline and a number of requests are being throttled even though our Dedicated+Reserved contract should cover peak QPS.

Impact: customers are seeing timeouts on payment confirmations (FastPay Checkout). We have a spike in production errors and are losing successful authorizations. This is customer-impacting now.

We pulled request IDs and attached a small sample plus perf snapshot. Ops is in the loop (ops@fastpay.com). Can you confirm whether this is a noisy neighbor / pool saturation or something on your reserved allocation side? We need ETA on remediation steps and whether you can route our traffic to a fallback model or increase headroom immediately.

Attached: perf_snapshot_0629.csv, request_samples_0629.txt

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Production Engineering
FastPay

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@fastpay.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High latency and 5xx spike — reserved throughput shortfall

Hi Elena — thanks for the quick heads-up and the attachments, they helped a lot.

Short summary from our first pass: we can see elevated queue depth and token latency on the dedicated GPU pool serving your reserved capacity in us-west-2 starting ~08:30 PDT (correlates with your timestamps). There is a persistent tail event that is consuming KV-cache and causing increased decode time for long sequences.

Immediate steps we are putting in motion now (t0–t15):
- Open an ops bridge and pause non-critical background jobs in that pool.
- Push a temporary routing rule to prefer a smaller, faster model variant for your checkout route (will reduce quality slightly but cut tail).
- Grant a two-hour burst authorization (we can enable now if you approve) to buy headroom while we diagnose root cause.

Can you confirm you can accept the temporary model fallback for the checkout path? If yes, we will flip the routing and monitor. Also please send any more request IDs you have (we already have the attachment). We will follow up with a root-cause timeline.

Linking a live dashboard so we can watch together: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/xyz/fastpay-inference-ops

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Ops triage: confirmed dedicated pool saturation in us-west-2

Team — ops summary after initial triage: we see a sustained increase in KV-cache misses and GPU decode time for sequences >1024 tokens starting at 08:28 PDT; this matches FastPay's checkout traffic pattern where occasional long-context requests spike. The dedicated pool serving FastPay's reserved capacity hit sustained utilization >95% across several nodes which triggered backpressure and token-level throttling.

Immediate remediation options (ordered by speed):
1) Enable emergency 2-hour burst (pre-authorized) -> add ephemeral capacity and increase headroom (T+5m to enable).
2) Push routing to smaller quantized model variant for checkout (T+3–7m) — lowest friction, minimal config change.
3) Apply soft-rate-limits to non-critical endpoints if FastPay agrees (T+10m).

We recommend 1+2 in parallel while we investigate root cause (noisy job? sudden traffic pattern change?). Marissa: this needs sales/exec sign-off for burst credit authorization. Karthik: please validate that fallback model will not require an offline reload or migration that could prolong the window.

I am attaching a short perf snapshot and request id list for correlation.

— David
Director, Inference Operations

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@fastpay.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High latency and 5xx spike — reserved throughput shortfall

Elena — per David's note above we are going to enable the temporary fallback model for checkout and provision a 2-hour burst immediately. Please confirm acceptance of the fallback (we will trim some long-tail content handling to reduce latency).

If you confirm, we will:
- Flip routing now and monitor (expected improvement in p99 in ~3–5 minutes).
- Provision burst for 2 hours; we will monitor usage and share a timeline for rollback.
- Start root-cause analysis (David/Karthik) and provide a remediation plan within 6 hours.

If you prefer not to use the fallback, we'll need authorization to provision burst and to apply soft-rate-limits to non-critical endpoints.

Thanks — apologies for the impact and we'll keep you updated every 15 minutes while this stabilizes.

— Sofia

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@fastpay.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fastpay.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High latency and 5xx spike — reserved throughput shortfall

Sofia / team — please proceed with the fallback model and the 2-hour burst. We approve temporary quality reduction for checkout to restore user-facing availability. Please share ETA and keep Ops on the bridge.

Elena
Head of Production Engineering, FastPay

---

(Internal update, 2026-07-01)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Exec notification & authorization — recommend burst credit approval

Quick update: FastPay accepted the fallback and the burst, customer-facing errors dropped immediately and p99 latency returned close to baseline within 6 minutes of the change. Ops is completing RCA.

Given the customer impact and strategic deal (FP-2026-Q2-Expansion), I recommend we approve the 2-hour burst credit and prepare a short exec readout for the CTO and VP Sales. Please capture the follow-ups:
- Root cause (KV-cache miss pattern + long sequence decoding) and long-term mitigations (model profiling + request-sampling controls).
- Proposed product changes: recommended model-variant pinning for known heavy routes and an automated headroom trigger for reserved pools.
- Customer impact and proposed commercial remediation (one month of burst credit and retrospective technical session).

Karthik/David/Sofia — please draft a one-pager by EOD and I will escalate to execs for sign-off.

— Marissa
Senior Director, Sales Engineering
